source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_source_reported.habit: Glabrous perennial herb from deep tough vertically or obliquely branched root
morphology_source_reported.stems: Prostrate to decumbent or ascending, 20–80 cm long
morphology_source_reported.leaves: Palmately compound, 4 leaflets usually 1–3 cm long, inconspicuously dotted; petiole length similar to leaflet length
morphology_source_reported.inflorescence: Long-peduncled axillary spikes with 3–10 well-spaced flowers
morphology_source_reported.bracts: Conspicuous paired elliptic-ovate bracts 7–15 mm long enclosing each flower
morphology_source_reported.fruits: Bristly pods 10–20 mm long, break into 2–6 segments
morphology_source_reported.diagnosis: Combination of 4 leaflets, large paired bracts and bristly jointed pods

habitat_source_reported: Sandy open woods and open areas, often low ground
cautions: Taxon concepts require independent name reconciliation before identification scoring
